If you haven't already read the basic rules for 5e you can find them hereBasic Rules . If online is your thing try roll20

I keep meaning to add helpful info for new players to the sidebar. Thanks for the reminder.

What @Egon said is a good bet. Meetup is a great way the find groups. Also, if you have a local hobby store (comic books, MTG cards, etc), see if they have a D&D Encounters night. People there would be a great resource both for learning the game, and finding people to play with.
Play online!! Go to roll20.net, click "look for game" and make sure to click the box that searches for groups that are newbie friendly.

Depending upon the city you live in, http://www.meetup.com seems to be a good place to start. Search it for DND groups and organizations and you'll usually find a few that have many members, some of who are seeking new players or starting new campaigns.

Hobby shops, as mentioned by others here, are also a good place to go. Someone mentioned asking about D&D Encounters, which is a good idea. Local stores will often run encounter nights which are basically a one-off adventure that you can play to get a feel for the game. These are usually very new-player-friendly, since they are almost designed around teaching the game and building people's interest.

My highest recommendation though, is to read the basic rules and get your friends into DnD. Get over the stigma, and slap any of your friends who start to act like they are too cool for DnD. I took the basic 5e rules I just linked and drug a few of my friends together who had never played before, (I hadn't either) and I forced them to play with me. It only took one time, and now we play often and I'm running a campaign that's lasted 8 months so far. Don't get daunted by the rules. The rules are bendable, and you learn them as you go. Get the basics down and start trying. There's no better way to really learn the way the game works than to play it, and it's not fun if you're too hung up on specifics. Just get into it and enter with an open mind!

Obviously, that might not be as easy as it sounds. I have plenty of friends that would not play at all, but I found enough who would that I managed to get something started. I just think it's worth a try, the game is more fun to learn if you're learning with an entire group. It's also much more fun if you're playing with people you like. I've played in games with strangers and most the time it's a great experience, but I also fear for people just starting to play who go to a meetup and get matched up with a bunch of weirdos who they aren't all that compatible with, and then judge the game based on that experience. D&D is about the community you're playing with and your shared imagination, and your rapport with them is integral to the enjoyment of the game. When you play with a bunch of jerks, it makes the game suck.

That's my two cents! Good luck!

edit: Also, it sounds sketchy, but I've actually had success posting on craigslist to find players or games. Search your local Craigslist for D&D and you might find a group seeking a player. The people who play D&D are usually pretty friendly to new people and will be more than willing to help you learn. If you don't find anything there, try just posting a "player looking for group" post. I've gotten emails that turned into games that way too.
